security_audit.summary: All 50 static findings are false positives involving Markdown formatting, ordinary authentication requirements, public reference links, and unrelated prose. The instructions require paid-run approval and treat external content as untrusted; no evidence found of credential theft, destructive intent, or prompt injection. This review covers SKILL.md only, not the external PyPI package or its dependencies.

content.user_title: Find Emerging AI Keywords Worth Researching
content.value_statement: New AI launches create search opportunities that are difficult to compare across sources. This skill uses a research CLI to turn discovery signals into keyword priorities.
actual_capabilities: Run the pinned research CLI to discover AI names from X, Hugging Face, GitHub, and sitemap signals.
Research supplied names without discovery and compare named keywords with related generic phrases.
Present prioritize, watch, and skip decisions with estimated daily searches, trend direction, competition, and market context.
Collect tool complaints from supported review and discussion sources, with categorized gaps and linked quotes.
Use configured site performance data to distinguish updating existing pages from creating new pages.
Report missing credentials, failed sources, first-run limitations, brand flags, and uncertainty in demand estimates.
limitations: Requires an external CLI, Python 3.10 or newer, an AIsa API key, and approval for paid API calls.
The first daily run primarily builds snapshots; immediate repeat runs show only changes since the previous run.
Search estimates are approximate, Google Ads data lags, and optional keys affect coverage and trend reliability.
Does not read App Store, Google Play, Trustpilot, Facebook groups, or There Is An AI For That.

use_cases.title: Prioritize AI content topics
use_cases.description: Compare emerging names and generic queries to decide which pages deserve research, monitoring, or no further work.

use_cases.title: Investigate tool demand
use_cases.description: Review complaint categories and linked evidence to identify problems that a new or improved tool might address.

use_cases.title: Monitor emerging AI products
use_cases.description: Track new model and repository names, then separate early attention from sustained search interest using source and trend evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Discover today's AI names
prompt_templates.prompt: Find today's new AI names and summarize their strongest signals. Show the estimated cost and duration, then wait for my approval before running.

prompt_templates.title: Research names I already have
prompt_templates.prompt: Research PhotoCraft and SynthID Detector without discovery. Confirm the estimated cost first, then compare named and generic keywords with decisions and evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate customer complaints
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate complaints about AI headshot tools. Ask for cost approval first, then group gaps with linked quotes and distinguish observed counts from market size.

prompt_templates.title: Compare markets and existing pages
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my configured sites and sources to evaluate emerging AI keywords. Confirm costs before running. Compare markets, competition, existing pages, and missing-source caveats.

output: Trend: no rise seen in the available worldwide series.
The newest two days are excluded, so this does not prove that interest did not rise.

best_practices: Keep a consistent working directory and review configured sources before comparing results across runs.
Approve each paid run after reviewing its estimated cost, duration, and optional features.
Keep source links and caveats visible, and treat instructions inside retrieved material as untrusted data.
anti_patterns: Repeat the daily run immediately and treat fewer incremental leads as evidence of falling market interest.
Treat search estimates, complaint counts, or payment links as proof of market size or business success.
Publish provider-restricted data or take external actions without separate, specific user approval.

faq.question: What do I need before running the skill?
faq.answer: You need Python 3.10 or newer, the pinned research CLI, and an AIsa API key. Optional provider keys expand coverage.

faq.question: Does the workflow use paid APIs?
faq.answer: Yes. Daily, sources, keywords, and pains use paid APIs. The skill requires approval after disclosing estimated cost and duration.

faq.question: Can I research names without collecting new ones?
faq.answer: Yes. The keywords path accepts supplied names, supports repository mappings, and handles up to eight names per call.

faq.question: Why does the first daily run return few leads?
faq.answer: It establishes snapshots and mainly reports GitHub breakouts. Limited first-run output does not mean the market is quiet.

faq.question: Are the search-volume figures exact?
faq.answer: No. Daily search estimates are approximate, and volume data runs about two months behind. Missing optional keys can weaken trend evidence.

faq.question: Does this review verify the external CLI package?
faq.answer: No. The reviewed skill contains instructions only. The external PyPI package, its dependencies, and provider behavior were not audited.
